req.title: Login required for delete
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they POST /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-014 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users who POST to /<id>/delete are redirected to /auth/login. The test suite must cover: (1) positive case — anonymous POST to a valid post id triggers a 302 redirect to /auth/login; (2) negative case — an authenticated user POSTing to /<id>/delete is NOT redirected to /auth/login (they can delete); (3) boundary case — anonymous POST to id=1 (the only existing post, boundary of valid ids) still redirects; plus additional cases for id=0 (below boundary) and a non-existent id to ensure the login_required decorator fires before any post-existence check. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (302 vs 200/302-to-index), exact Location header strings, and testing both sides of the authentication state transition.

tests.name: test_anonymous_post_delete_redirects_to_login
preconditions: App is initialised with test database containing post id=1
No user is logged in (anonymous session)
actions: POST to /1/delete without any session cookie
trace: R-FLASKR-014: anonymous POST /<id>/delete must redirect to /auth/login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_anonymous_post_delete_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_anonymous_post_delete_redirects_to_login()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_authenticated_post_delete_does_not_redirect_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    assert r.headers['Location'] != '/auth/login'

tests.name: test_state_transition_logout_then_delete_redirects_to_login
preconditions: App is initialised with test database containing post id=1
User 'test' logs in, then logs out (returns to anonymous state)
expected: Location header equals /auth/login (not / or any other path)
trace: R-FLASKR-014: STC — after logout the user is anonymous; subsequent POST /<id>/delete must redirect to /auth/login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_state_transition_logout_then_delete_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    logout_r = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert logout_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_state_transition_logout_then_delete_redirects_to_login()

tests.name: test_decision_table_other_user_anonymous_vs_authenticated
preconditions: App is initialised with test database; post id=1 belongs to user 'test'
Two decision paths: anonymous user and authenticated-but-wrong-author user
actions: POST /1/delete with no session (anonymous) — expect redirect to /auth/login
POST /auth/login as 'other' (not the author), then POST /1/delete — expect 403, not redirect to /auth/login
expected: Authenticated non-author: status 403 (login_required passes, get_post author check fails)
trace: R-FLASKR-014: DT — distinguishes anonymous (redirect to login) from authenticated-wrong-author (403); confirms login_required is the gate
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_decision_table_other_user_anonymous_vs_authenticated():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    anon_r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert anon_r.status_code == 302
    assert anon_r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'other', 'password': 'other'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    auth_r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert auth_r.status_code == 403
    assert auth_r.headers.get('Location', '') != '/auth/login'

test_decision_table_other_user_anonymous_vs_authenticated()
